gap: No result ChatGPT got works out the full inverter-plus-battery hardware cost per kWh together with solar refill hours from each unit's own PV input. At today's maker-store prices the EG4 FlexBOSS21 + PowerPro is $470 per nominal kWh but $588 per usable kWh at EG4's 80% DoD, against $525/kWh for the Anker SOLIX E10 with two batteries and $643/kWh for the EcoFlow DELTA Pro Ultra X bundle. The best case for a full refill on the unit's own solar input is 0.54 h for EG4, 0.68 h for Powerwall 3, 1.23 h for DPU X and 1.37 h for E10.
standout_why: I read energysage.com/best-batteries-for-whole-home-backup (cited), itechguides Powerwall alternatives (cited) and solutionenergy.com/batteries (cited). EnergySage gives installed $/kWh for Powerwall 3 ($998), aPower 2 ($1,177) and EG4 WallMount ($1,163), and no solar input figures. itechguides gives specs plus DPU prices but no $/kWh and no refill hours. SolutionEnergy gives $/kWh for plug-in kits only, assuming 85% is usable (DPU about $683, Anker about $651, using older prices), and backup hours at stated loads. It does not price the EG4 inverter and battery as one system and does not compute solar refill time. None of the three pages computes Wh per lb or solar kW per stored kWh.
decides: Among products with a public price, the EG4 FlexBOSS21 + PowerPro is cheapest per nameplate kWh and has the most solar input per kWh (21 kW PV for 14.3 kWh), which supports ChatGPT's 'best value' label. Counted per usable kWh at EG4's own 80% DoD, though, it is $588/kWh and loses to the Anker SOLIX E10 + 2 batteries at $525/kWh, a product Dealectric already sells through rakuten:ankersolix and ChatGPT never showed. ChatGPT's card for the EcoFlow DELTA Pro Ultra is out of date: the original is listed out of stock on us.ecoflow.com at $3,799, and the bundle on sale now is the DELTA Pro Ultra X at $7,899. Powerwall 3 is the only true single enclosure here, and it is 46.4 Wh per lb including its inverter, but it has no public price to compare.
